text:
maria: Hey team — Quantus (new HW partner) is offering an early-access hardware drop next week for us to run our benchmark suite & give feedback. They require a signed NDA before hardware handoff. Need to coordinate: who runs the bench, what infra we need, telemetry/safety limits, and PR/announcement timing. @david @sophie any capacity next week? :eyes:
david: I can take primary ownership of the benchmark run. Would like to reuse the inference-bench harness. Can we get a list of expected images/firmware and whether they'll provide a Docker runtime or raw node?
chris_quantus: Hi all — Chris from Quantus here. NDA link: https://quantus.example/nda (we'll send official email too). Shipping 4xunits (A100-class replacement) on Mon. We'll provide a prebuilt container (quantus/runtime:1.0) + a host kernel driver. Firmware v42.3. We can also provide a flash image if you want local install. Happy to join kickoff.
sophie: Good to know. For runtime: does the container expose NVME and pass-through /dev devices? We'll need SSH + root for kernel driver install. Can you confirm kernel support (5.10 / 5.15) and if DKMS modules are needed? Also any special PCIe VF config?
chris_quantus: Container uses device mounts (NVME, /dev/nvme*, /dev/quantus0). Kernel support: tested on 5.10 & 5.15. DKMS optional — we ship a prebuilt module and instructions in /opt/quantus/driver. No special VF config unless you're doing multi-tenant pinning.
erik: Legal note: please ensure NDA includes permission to run benchmarks and share aggregated results with partners. We need explicit embargo window for co-announcement and a clause about telemetry — what telemetry will Quantus collect from our runs?
maria: Good call. @chris_quantus can you add telemetry detail in the NDA or separate MSA? Quantus — what metrics/telemetry do you capture from the host and container (CPU, nvme health, hw counters, model traces)?
chris_quantus: We collect system metrics (CPU, mem, nvme SMART), driver logs, and optional HW perf counters. No model payloads or token-level traces unless explicitly enabled. All telemetry stored on Quantus S3 and we can set retention. We'll add a telemetry appendix to the NDA.
david: For bench spec: we'll run 3 workloads — chat (gpt-like), long-context encoding, and embedding throughput. Plan: run our standard inference-bench with the following profile: 
```
models: [redwood/ggml-13b, open/llama-70b]
seqs: [512, 2048, 8192]
batch: [1, 8, 16]
metrics: [p50_latency, p99_latency, tokens_sec, power_watts]
```
Need to know power measurement capability (PMBus?) and if you can provide a rack-level PDUs reading.
sophie: Also confirm whether KV-cache eviction behaves differently on Quantus. If their runtime pipelines kv cache to NVMe, we need to capture that in configs. Can we get their recommended quantization knobs?
rachel: From GTM: if the bench looks good, marketing would like a joint case study + co-announcement. We typically request a 2-week embargo after we finalize numbers. Any objections?
maria: Sounds fine. Let's aim for: NDA signed by Friday, hardware shipped Mon, bench run Tue-Wed, results validation Thu, internal review Fri, then 2-week embargo if both parties approve.
erik: I will review NDA drafts and flag any telemetry/data retention redlines.
chris_quantus: I'll update the NDA with telemetry appendix and send an ops-runbook + SSH keys instructions by EOD. Happy to set a 30-min kickoff Tue morning.
david: I'll prepare the bench container and a small infra playbook (ssh keys, target users, power metering). If anyone has special test prompts or regression prompts, pls drop them here.
sophie: I'll schedule a runtime engineer to be on-call during the run (me + 1). Also will test driver install in a local VM image ahead of hardware arrival if Chris provides the flash image.
maria: Thanks all. Action items: 1) Chris — send NDA + ops runbook (by EOD) 2) Erik — legal review (ASAP) 3) David — bench harness prep + infra notes 4) Sophie — runtime oncall + pretest 5) Rachel — draft co-announcement timeline. Update in this thread once NDA is sent. :thumbsup:
